message.content: {"caption":"A twelve-panel line-chart dashboard compares accuracy across math and code benchmarks and their averages over a shared numeric horizontal axis.","description":"The picture is a grid of 12 small line charts, with three columns and four rows. Every panel has Accuracy on the vertical axis and an unlabeled numeric horizontal axis marked at 50, 100, 150, 200, 250, 300, and 350; the plotted lines extend to about 380. Each chart has one line, a pale shaded area beneath it, and its own vertical scale. No legend or printed point values are shown, so the values in chart_values are estimated from the lines at the horizontal-axis ticks. The first two rows use blue lines: AIME 2024 and AIME 2025 fluctuate sharply at low accuracy; Olympiad Bench generally rises from about 0.26 to around 0.41; Minerva rises overall from about 0.28 to around 0.42 with dips; Math 500 rises from about 0.50 to the mid-0.70s; and AMC 2023 is highly variable, with sharp peaks and troughs. The orange CODE REASONING row contains HumanEval+, MBPP+, and LiveCodeBench: HumanEval+ fluctuates mostly around 0.72–0.76, with a brief high near 0.78 and a later dip near 0.71; MBPP+ stays comparatively steady around 0.68–0.72 and trends slightly lower near the end; LiveCodeBench varies around 0.32–0.37. The bottom row, headed OVERALL PERFORMANCE, shows Math Average in blue, Code Average in orange, and Overall Average in green. Math Average rises overall from roughly 0.29 to 0.42 but has dips; Code Average remains comparatively level near 0.58–0.61; Overall Average generally rises from about 0.44 to about 0.50, with fluctuations.
